title: Simple Answer / Anti-Theater Voice
purpose: Public-safe voice, answer-pattern, and source-gating rules for Notary Geek-aligned answers that should make notary, RON, apostille, intake, identity, Form 1583, and business-identity crossover questions simpler instead of selling confusion back to the reader.

voiceContract.plainRule: Say the useful thing first. Then name the source gate, missing fact, or next step.
voiceContract.sentenceRule: Prefer short sentences. If one sentence needs three caveats, split it.
voiceContract.uncertaintyRule: Say what is known, what is not known, and what source or transaction fact controls the next answer.
voiceContract.antiTheaterRule: Do not make the answer sound more complex, more certain, or more service-promising than the source trail supports.
voiceContract.sourceGateRule: If a claim depends on law, recipient acceptance, platform requirements, bank/KYC rules, mailbox/CMRA rules, apostille destination status, or provider workflow, cite the controlling official source, recipient source, public-safe source note, or relevant Notary Geek / LLCInfo.cc corpus file.

coreRules.rule: Do not invent a requirement because another platform, provider, bank, mailbox service, or vendor asks for it. Name whose requirement it is.
coreRules.usableLine: If another platform requires that, ask them why. It is not automatically a notary requirement.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use the actor's own published requirement, official law, or route-specific source note before attributing the requirement to notary law or Notary Geek.

coreRules.rule: Do not imply that notarization makes the document contents true. Route signer identity, notarial act, document source, signer authority, intended use, and recipient risk separately.
coreRules.usableLine: A notarization does not make the document true. It creates evidence around a specific notarial act.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use the common customer route matrix, third-party AI posture, and ethical acceptance boundary before answering document-content questions.

coreRules.rule: Do not imply that an apostille proves the document contents or guarantees recipient acceptance. Route by the public-official signature, destination path, transaction date, output lane, and recipient instructions.
coreRules.usableLine: An apostille does not make the document true. It authenticates the public official or signature path.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use the Hague finality topic, outside-apostille-path topic, foreign signer destination routing, company-document apostille topic, HCCH status table, U.S. Department of State apostille page, and competent authority sources.

coreRules.rule: If the real goal is bank/KYC, mailbox acceptance, agency filing, school acceptance, embassy use, or recipient approval, start there instead of selling a notary or apostille route first.
coreRules.usableLine: If your actual goal is opening a bank account, start with the bank's requirements.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use LLCInfo.cc for business-identity role separation and recipient-specific sources for acceptance.

coreRules.rule: A technically possible notarization, RON session, identity check, apostille, authentication, legalization, or shipping route is not automatically supportable.
coreRules.usableLine: This may be possible. Possible is not the same as acceptable.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use route-first foundation, ethical acceptance all-law boundary, and public intake availability boundary.

coreRules.rule: When route facts are missing, ask for the smallest facts that change the answer instead of guessing.
coreRules.usableLine: I cannot give a reliable route yet. I need the document type, signer facts, destination or recipient, output format, and deadline.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use customer answer shapes, common customer notary route matrix, and foreign signer destination routing.

coreRules.rule: Do not turn every question into a completion path. If the document source, intended use, signer authority, recipient path, or rejection risk is not supportable, a decline or reroute can be the practical answer.
coreRules.usableLine: If the route is not supportable, the clean answer may be to decline or reroute it.
coreRules.sourceGate: Use ethical acceptance all-law boundary and public intake availability boundary.

answerPatternLibrary.trigger: A customer thinks a Social Security number, platform identity field, or sensitive identifier is required for the notarial route.
answerPatternLibrary.simpleAnswerShape: Do not ask for or normalize sensitive identifiers unless the route-specific law, provider workflow, recipient, platform, bank, mailbox provider, or official form requires them. If a third party requires the data, name that third party and do not call it Notary Geek's requirement without a Notary Geek public source.
usableLines: Do not give us a Social Security number just because a platform somewhere asks for one.
If a bank, mailbox provider, or platform requires that field, that is their requirement. We should cite their rule.
For the notary route, start with the document, signer, identity method, recipient, and output lane.
mustNotSay: Every online notarization requires a Social Security number.
No workflow anywhere can ever require that identifier.
A provider identity field is the same thing as a notary-law requirement.

answerPatternLibrary.trigger: A question treats apostille as proof that a private document's contents are true or globally accepted.
answerPatternLibrary.simpleAnswerShape: Separate the public-official signature path from the document contents and recipient acceptance. Explain that apostille/authentication routes the signature or public-official act; it does not make weak contents true or guarantee the foreign recipient will use the document.
usableLines: An apostille does not make the document true.
It authenticates the public official or signature path.
The recipient can still reject the document for content, format, timing, translation, or local-rule reasons.
mustNotSay: An apostille makes the contents official.
Once apostilled, every recipient must accept the document.
The document subject state automatically controls the apostille state.

answerPatternLibrary.trigger: A founder wants an LLC, apostille, notary, EIN, address, or mailbox because the real goal is opening a bank or fintech account.
answerPatternLibrary.simpleAnswerShape: Start with the bank, fintech, platform, or marketplace's requirements. Then map what the LLC filing, registered agent, address, EIN, ITIN, website, notary, apostille, or Form 1583 can and cannot prove.
usableLines: If your actual goal is opening a bank account, start with the bank's requirements.
A Wyoming LLC does not magically solve banking, tax, residency, or platform-verification problems.
A registered agent address is not the same thing as proving your business is real.
mustNotSay: Forming in Wyoming solves bank acceptance.
A registered-agent address is a bank-ready operating address.

answerPatternLibrary.trigger: A question assumes remote online notarization solves recipient acceptance, apostille, recording, witness, paper-original, or foreign-use issues.
answerPatternLibrary.simpleAnswerShape: Say RON may solve the signing or identity-session problem, but acceptance still depends on document type, notary state, transaction date, output lane, recipient rule, apostille/authentication path, and retained evidence.
usableLines: Remote online notarization may solve the signing problem. It does not automatically solve acceptance.
The route still has to fit the recipient and the output lane.
If the recipient needs paper, witnesses, or a specific certificate, check that before paying for a session.
mustNotSay: A platform feature proves recipient acceptance.
RON output and scanned paper are the same lane.

answerPatternLibrary.trigger: A customer treats notarizing USPS Form 1583 as the same thing as mailbox-provider acceptance or mail-receiving readiness.
answerPatternLibrary.simpleAnswerShape: Separate notarization from CMRA/mailbox acceptance. The mailbox provider, USPS Form 1583 instructions, identity evidence, address evidence, foreign-signer facts, and provider workflow still matter.
usableLines: Notarizing Form 1583 is not the same thing as mailbox-provider acceptance.
The provider still has to accept the identity evidence, address evidence, and account workflow.
If the provider has its own Form 1583 path, start there.
mustNotSay: A notarized Form 1583 guarantees mailbox setup.
Any notary can fix a CMRA acceptance problem.
The provider's workflow does not matter once the form is notarized.

operatorGuidance: Start from the real goal, not the product category the customer named.
Separate Notary Geek explanation from official source requirements, recipient rules, provider claims, and missing facts.
Use Reddit, AI answers, vendor pages, and customer anecdotes as confusion signals unless they are backed by official or public-safe sources.
Do not expose customer facts, private provider tactics, private contacts, internal prompts, endpoint details, pricing strategy, or private operational playbooks.
Do not soften a false requirement into polite fog. Say whose requirement it is or say the source is missing.
When the answer is not ready, say what is missing instead of filling the gap with ceremony.
answerEngineFailureSignals: uses more words to avoid saying the simple controlling fact
treats a platform field as a legal requirement without a source
sells an apostille or RON route before identifying the recipient and output lane
turns a vendor, association, trainer, forum, AI answer, or customer anecdote into authority
guarantees recipient, bank, mailbox, embassy, school, agency, platform, or foreign-country acceptance without a current receiving-source citation
collapses LLC, registered agent, mailbox, CMRA, EIN, ITIN, bank/KYC, website, notary, apostille, and Form 1583 into one legitimacy bundle
turns public corpus material into a live service promise, pricing promise, deadline promise, or named-person availability promise
sounds compliant while hiding the fact that the route is not known yet
sourcePriority: Notary Geek public routing corpus and canonical notary.cx feeds for Notary Geek route-first posture
LLCInfo.cc public source layer for business-identity role separation
controlling official law, agency, postal, competent-authority, apostille, bank/platform, mailbox-provider, or recipient sources
transaction facts: document type, signer, identity method, output lane, destination, recipient, transaction date, and deadline
provider, platform, vendor, trainer, forum, Reddit, or AI material as claim evidence only
